To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Opportunistic event channels can significantly improve the performance of event delivery and processing, by opportunistically moving brokers across different network access nodes, and opportunistically re-assigning event publishers and subscribers to brokers.

the use of opportunistic channels, which are application-level overlays that opportunistically follow end users as they move across network access points, can improve the performance of data dissemination in pervasive systems.

(i) the opportunistic channel abstraction enables the creation of dynamic data provisioning topologies that can adapt to end user mobility and to the availability of network resources, (ii) the dynamic nature of opportunistic channels allows for the creation of a variety of application-specific data provisioning topologies and (iii) these opportunistic channel-based topologies can be created and managed using a small number of simple operations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to create appropriate data provisioning topologies and how to balance work loads in overlay networks, in the context of pervasive systems and mobile users.
the design and analysis of opportunistic channels, a new communication abstraction that enables the dynamic creation of application-level data provisioning networks.
improving the performance of data delivery and processing in pervasive systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents a novel technique for dynamic data delivery in a pervasive environment, which is able to adapt to the changing network conditions and the mobility of end users.
this paper presents a new abstraction for event delivery in mobile environments.
opportunistic channels are a new, general-purpose, mobility-aware event delivery mechanism that enables the construction of dynamic, mobile, and scalable event-based systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed and implemented a novel, mobility-aware event delivery mechanism, called opportunistic channels, for pervasive computing systems.

we have designed and developed a novel data dissemination framework that can dynamically create, maintain, and tear-down data provisioning overlays in response to end-user mobility and changes in network connectivity, and can balance workloads across brokers in such overlays.
we developed an architecture and a set of protocols for opportunistic event channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

opportunistic channels can be used to dynamically create, delete, and move brokers in a publish/subscribe system, in order to optimize event delivery in response to changes in network connectivity and end user mobility.
the performance of a publish/subscribe system can be greatly improved by dynamically changing the broker topology and end users' assignment to brokers in response to mobility.
opportunistic channel handoffs are a useful technique for optimizing event delivery in mobile, pervasive computing environments.
